sources.title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook 5.3.1 What are the objectives?
sources.version: Retained original HTML inspected 2026-10-16; live URL returned HTTP403 on independent refetch
sources.locator: 5.3.1 opening objectives paragraphs and Types of designs
sources.excerpt: Planning an experiment begins with carefully considering what the objectives (or goals) are.
sources.scope: Supports defining purpose and selecting factors/responses/design; no claim about this model results.

sources.title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook 5.3.3.2 Randomized block designs
sources.version: Retained original HTML inspected 2026-10-16; live URL returned HTTP403 on independent refetch
sources.locator: Opening Blocking to remove effect of nuisance factors and Blocking used for nuisance factors that can be controlled
sources.excerpt: The basic concept is to create homogeneous blocks in which the nuisance factors are held constant and the factor of interest is allowed to vary.
sources.scope: Supports controlling data/initialization/work/checkpoint-selection confounds; does not claim matching all factors is always feasible.

sources.title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook 7.2.6.2 Percentiles
sources.version: Retained original HTML inspected 2026-10-16; live URL returned HTTP403 on independent refetch
sources.locator: Definition of percentiles; Estimation of percentiles; small-sample example
sources.excerpt: Order statistics provide a way of estimating proportions of the data that should fall above and below a given value, called a percentile.
sources.scope: Sample percentile is an estimator, not a deployment latency guarantee; this review makes no new statistical interval claim.

sources.title: RouteLLM: Learning to Route LLMs with Preference Data
sources.locator: 2.1 Problem Formulation, 2.2 Metrics equations3–7, 4.5 Routing Overhead Table7
sources.excerpt: Neither of these metrics alone is sufficient, as they do not capture the quality-cost trade-off in routing.
sources.scope: Supports joint cost-quality evaluation, routing before seeing outputs, and separately accounting controller overhead; its dollar/GPU results are not transferred to this CPU model.

sources.title: PyTorch CUDA semantics — Memory management
sources.version: PyTorch 2.8 documentation, retained original HTML inspected 2026-10-16
sources.excerpt: You can use memory_allocated() and max_memory_allocated() to monitor memory occupied by tensors, and use memory_reserved() and max_memory_reserved() to monitor the total amount of memory managed by the caching allocator.
sources.scope: Only supports distinction between tensor allocation/peak and allocator reservation; no PyTorch2.14 CUDA execution or GPU memory number claimed.
